reasons: The cited Section 4(a) grants a mutual for-any-reason exit on 90 days' notice after a one-year Initial Term; the 90-day Customer notice sits squarely inside the fallback's 60–90 day window, so 'compliant at the fallback' is the correct classification and no redline is warranted.
Walk-away triggers are not met: the term is a 1-year auto-renewing term (not a multi-year lock-in), and Vendor's convenience right requires the same 90 days' notice, i.e. not 'fewer than 90 days'.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing artifact — the right is drafted as 'Either Party may terminate ... for any reason', which includes the Customer — so it does not undermine the finding.

Economics are consistent with the fallback: Kubient's entitlement to fees 'generated during the termination period' is bounded by the ~3-month notice period under a revenue-share model rather than an uncapped early-termination penalty.

Shortfalls from the preferred position (90 rather than 30 days' notice, Vendor's right not confined to term-end, no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than flagged as deviations, per the playbook's minor sub-element rule.
Consistent with compliant-status expectations: no redline and no counterparty comment were produced, and the rendered text is unchanged from the original paragraph.
